text: Electron-beam lithography is the vehicle for research prototyping, photonic crystals, and inverse-designed geometries. What is its defining trade-off relative to optical projection lithography?
choices: Higher throughput but coarser (~1 micron) resolution
It needs no vacuum but requires expensive masks
5-10 nm resolution with zero mask cost, but serial write time (hours per chip) and 10-30 nm stitching errors
It can pattern only metals, not dielectrics
explanation: E-beam direct-write reaches 5-10 nm with no mask, ideal for prototypes and inverse-designed shapes, but it writes serially (t = DA/I; hours per chip, weeks per wafer) and suffers 10-30 nm write-field stitching errors that become scattering/phase defects. Choice 0 inverts the trade-off; choice 1 is wrong (e-beam needs high vacuum and uses no mask); choice 3 is false.
